summary: Hansa Teutonica is a lean, cutthroat network-building game where you race to claim trade routes with only two actions per turn, and can bump rival pieces off routes to steal their position. It rewards efficient upgrading of personal abilities as much as raw map presence.
praised: high replayability with multiple viable strategies
criticised: can feel mean when pieces get bumped back to supply
some upkeep tracking bonuses slows new players

interaction.detail: Players compete for the same routes and cities on a shared map, and can knock a rival's piece back to their personal supply to take their spot. Upgrade tracks and general stock remain private, but the map itself is fully contested.

scoring.why: Points come from completed routes, city presence bonuses, upgrade track completion, and endgame network bonuses, so efficient action use across all of these decides the winner.
scoring.how_you_win: You use your limited actions to claim trade routes and upgrade your abilities faster than opponents, banking points from routes and bonuses to finish with the highest total.
